title: Numbers
objective: Distinguish int from float and convert numbers to strings safely.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Eric Matthes
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Python has two everyday number types. An int is a whole number with no decimal point, like 5 or -12. A float has a decimal point, like 5.0 or 3.14, even if the digits after the point are zero.

Doing math with two ints gives an int (except division with /, which always gives a float). Mixing an int and a float in the same expression gives a float, because Python widens to the more precise type.
You cannot concatenate a number directly to a string with + — Python raises a TypeError. The fix is str(), which converts a number into its text form so it can be joined with other text.
explanation.rule: Use str(number) to convert a number into text before joining it to a string with +.

assignment.title: Ingot Count
assignment.brief: Write ingot_report(count) that prints the exact text 'Ingots: ' followed by count, using str() to combine them with +.
requirements: Concatenate with + and print the result, e.g. 'Ingots: 4' for count=4.
assignment.starterCode:
def ingot_report(count):
    # Build and print 'Ingots: ' + count using str().
    pass

ingot_report(4)
assignment.solutionCode:
def ingot_report(count):
    message = "Ingots: " + str(count)
    print(message)

ingot_report(4)

hints: You can't concatenate 'Ingots: ' directly to count — convert it first.
str(count) turns the number into text.
Join the pieces with + and print the combined string.
There is exactly one space after the colon in 'Ingots: '.
